finding:
The fourth bullet asserts that the full S_I(G), in the topology just defined, is a strict LF-space, nuclear, complete and Montel, for every second-countable Hausdorff locally compact abelian G with a continuous proper surjective module ν:G→ℝ_{>0} and every nonempty real interval I, including singletons and intervals not containing zero. Its parentheticals describe applications, not a general bounded-lifting or trace assertion. Theorem D.3.3.7 uses a chosen continuous homomorphic section, whose existence in this setting is claimed in Remark D.2.1.2. The section gives coordinates G/k ≅ ℝ_{>0}×(G¹/k), where G¹=ker ν; it is not data in the function membership, weighted maps, or limit topology of the introductory bullet. The proof of item (2) on p. 810 appeals to Example D.3.3.5 for the nuclear Fréchet stages and to countable strict-limit permanence; this does not require item (1)'s tensor isomorphism. The later consequences in (2), including its conditional nuclear Fréchet specialization, are not additional conclusions in the assigned bullet.

The indexing is by compact subgroups k with compactly generated annihilator in the full Pontryagin dual, as printed on p. 11 and at the start of Definition D.3.3.3. Every compact k lies in G¹ since ℝ_{>0} has no nontrivial compact subgroup. The full annihilator contains the pullback of the radial dual ℝ and is uncountable, so it cannot literally be finitely generated. The 'finitely generated orthogonal' in the limit paragraph on p. 805 must be read in light of the explicit p. 804 comparison: after splitting, k^⊥ identifies with ℝ times the annihilator in the discrete dual of G¹, and finite generation refers to that discrete factor. It does not shrink the full-dual indexing to an empty family.

The first missing Lean object is S(G/k) on all admissible quotients, with its transported Schwartz–Bruhat seminorms, including angular derivatives in torus directions. The p. 11 smoothness condition and the p. 804 continuity formulation agree on a stage: a weighted Schwartz profile on G/k for one a∈I can be divided by its smooth nonvanishing weight there. The weighted stage consists of a single common k-invariant profile φ with ν^aφ in S(G/k) for every a∈I; its topology is induced by φ↦(ν^aφ)_a into the product of those actual Schwartz–Bruhat spaces. A group quotient, a bare space of smooth functions, independent coordinates for each weight, or the pointwise function topology does not give this object. For example, G=ℝ_{>0}×𝕋 with projection module and k trivial is admissible (dual ℝ×ℤ). If b is a nonzero smooth compactly supported function of log t, φ(t,z)=b(log t)z is in the stage for I=[1,3] and is not radial. Its periodic lift in the angular coordinate cannot be an ordinary Schwartz function on ℝ², since at a fixed log t with b nonzero the modulus does not tend to zero as the angular lift tends to infinity. Mathlib's SchwartzMap requires a normed real vector domain and full polynomial decay in that domain; ContMDiffMap supplies smoothness but not the mixed seminorm topology. No uniform quotient-space bridge providing the needed function spaces and seminorms was found.

The second missing object is the actual locally convex inductive limit of those weighted stages along the canonical pullbacks for k′⊆k. One needs their union as functions on G, with the finest locally convex vector topology making all stage inclusions continuous (equivalently, the seminorms continuous on every actual weighted stage), not just an algebraic colimit, a pointwise topology, or the fixed-stage weighted product topology. Strict LF then concerns a countable Fréchet presentation with topological embeddings, not strict increase of every stage. Both completeness and the Montel conditions refer to this same limit topology. Pinned Mathlib has CompleteSpace, MontelSpace (closed von Neumann bounded sets are compact), BarrelledSpace, and strong-dual infrastructure. The manuscript also says 'Montel' includes strong-bidual reflexivity, so the Mathlib Heine–Borel class alone should not be substituted for that convention; this is not a claim that Montel is unrepresentable. Nuclearity is a separate missing interface: no genuine locally convex nuclearity definition matching C.2.4.1 or C.2.4.2 was found in project or pinned Mathlib. PiTensorProduct.projectiveSeminorm works with seminormed inputs, not two general locally convex topologies, and its deprecated, extensionally equal injectiveSeminorm is explicitly not the mathematical injective construction. Equating these surrogates, or equating nuclearity with completeness or compactness of bounded sets, would not state this assertion.
